q0024.answer: Works are classified primarily as original works and repairs and maintenance. Original works cover all new construction, additions and alterations to existing works, reconstruction of entire structures after wear or calamity, and repairs to newly purchased or abandoned buildings needed to make them usable. Repairs and maintenance cover the operations needed from time to time to keep existing property in satisfactory state when complete reconstruction is not necessary, and are further divided into ordinary and special repairs.
q0024.source: Kerala Financial Code Vol I, Article 164

quotes.text: Original works include all new construction, whether of entirely new works or of additions and alterations to existing works, reconstruction of entire structures necessitated by wear and tear or by damage due to some calamity and all repairs to newly purchased or previously abandoned buildings required to make them usable.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 164 Classification of works

quotes.text: Repairs and maintenance include all the operations required from time to time to maintain existing properties in a satisfactory state and make good the damage due to wear and tear, when complete reconstruction is not necessary.
quotes.ref: KFC Vol I, Art. 164 Classification of works

q0024.q: What are Original works and Maintenance works ?

q0284.answer: Normally a Treasury Officer cannot pay a reward or honorarium to a gazetted officer until the Accountant General has intimated the rate of payment. However, honorarium paid to a gazetted government servant by the Kerala Public Service Commission is a listed exception, so such payment without the Accountant General's authorisation is not irregular.
q0284.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, Rule 18 and exception (b)

quotes.text: No withdrawal shall be permitted in order to meet the pay, leave salary, or allowances of a gazetted government servant or a reward or honorarium payable to a gazetted government servant
(b) for payment of honorarium to gazetted government servant by the Kerala Public Service Commission.

q0284.q: A treasury officer paid the honorarium sanctioned by the Public Service Commission to Gazetted officer without the authorisation of the Accountant General.

q0296.answer: True. Each Disbursing Officer must maintain a register of expenditure and liabilities in Form KBM 12, and report the expenditure and liabilities monthly to the superior controlling authority.

quotes.text: each disbursing Officer should maintain a register of expenditure and liabilities, in Form KBM 12.
quotes.ref: Kerala Budget Manual, Para 70(1) Disbursing Officers

q0296.q: Each disbursing officer is required to maintain a register of Expenditure and Liabilities.

q0302.answer: This is irregular. An earnest money deposit can never be repaid in part; it must be refunded in full on a proper refund order.
q0302.source: Kerala Treasury Code Vol I, refund of deposits

quotes.text: An earnest money deposit shall never be repaid in part.
quotes.ref: KTC Vol I, rule on repayment of deposits (earnest money deposit)

q0302.q: A Treasury Officer permitted part payment of an earnest money deposit.
